purpose: Define the observable behavior of crates/core::extractor: given a single .tsx, .ts, or .d.ts source file, it walks the OXC AST once and produces a SourceData containing zero or more ComponentMapping entries (component name -> props type name) plus zero or more diagnostics, without any AST reference outliving the parse_file() call.
scope: Component detection within a single source file for the recognized authoring patterns: six FC-family type annotations (AC-001), forwardRef (AC-002), call-expression HOC-wrap around an already-collected identifier (AC-003), declared-no-init ForwardRefExoticComponent (AC-004), bare-identifier rename-alias (AC-005), call-expression HOC-wrap around an inline typed function/arrow (AC-006), call-expression HOC-wrap around a nested forwardRef call (AC-007), an inline union/intersection/object-literal props type synthesized into an anonymous alias (AC-024), a no-initializer binding carrying one of the six FC-family annotations (AC-025), and a post-file-scan `displayName` reassignment renaming a recognized component's mapping key (AC-027). Full detector precedence, evaluated in this order against the (cast-peeled, per AC-003's cast-peeling note) declarator: (1) AC-001's six FC-family annotations — checked against the declarator's own type annotation, independent of whatever the initializer is or whether one exists at all, and outranking every other pattern when present; (2) AC-002 forwardRef/React.forwardRef with 2+ type arguments; (3) AC-006 inline-function/arrow first-argument call wrap and AC-007 nested-forwardRef first-argument call wrap; (4) AC-003 identifier-first-argument call wrap and AC-005 bare-identifier alias. The file-source-type gate applies to all patterns except AC-004 (`.tsx` and `.d.ts` on, plain `.ts` off; AC-004 alone applies in all three, including plain `.ts` — see AC-008). The `as`-cast-peeling rule applies uniformly before AC-002, AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, and AC-007 are evaluated (not AC-001, which reads the declarator's own annotation). The named type reference consumed by AC-001, AC-004, and AC-006 is recorded by name only and never resolved against a declaration in this file or any other — it may be locally declared or imported; no same-file-declaration requirement exists. The diagnostic call sites: SkippedCandidate at Info severity (malformed built-in generic on a component-shaped alias — AC-009; an unmatched PascalCase binding with an initializer — AC-010; an unmatched PascalCase function declaration — AC-011; the forward-reference case of the wrap/rename patterns — AC-014); the single source-level pre-parse nesting-depth guard (byte-scan, threshold 2000, diagnostic code ExcessiveNesting at Error severity, whole-file skip — AC-012); the parser-error diagnostic paths, split by whether the parser panics (code ParseError, Error severity — AC-022 for the non-panicking, continuation case, AC-026 for the panicking, whole-file-empty case); the type-collection recursion guard (per-type-annotation counter, threshold 200, diagnostic code MaxDepthExceeded, Warning severity, truncation-to-source-text, one diagnostic per over-deep node — AC-023). JSDoc-to-declaration association including its destination fields, its exact delimiter-stripping rules, its proximity threshold, its single-consumption rule, and its exception for the declared-no-init pattern; the multi-alias case where several bindings alias the same base component; the documented silent-omission patterns that produce no ComponentMapping and no diagnostic; behavior on an empty source file; and the invariant that no AST-borrowed reference escapes parse_file().
non_goals: Anonymous default-exported function components (export default function(props) {}) — known, deliberately unsupported gap.
Class components and class-expression components — known, deliberately unsupported gap.
satisfies-wrapped expressions — known, deliberately unsupported gap.
Component detection or SkippedCandidate wiring for file extensions other than .tsx, .ts, and .d.ts (e.g. .jsx, .js, .mts, .cts) is not specified here.
Runtime validation of prop values or JSX usage is out of scope; the extractor only inspects declaration-level TypeScript/JSX syntax.
Cross-file component resolution (a component imported from another module and re-exported) is out of scope; only same-file identifier references are covered by AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, and AC-007.

Precedence or collision behavior when two declarations in the same file would each independently produce a component_mappings entry under the same component name (e.g. a function declaration and a forwardRef binding both named `Card`) is unconfirmed and explicitly out of scope for this spec. No merge, overwrite, or error rule is defined; implementers must not invent one. (This is distinct from AC-021's multi-alias case, which is confirmed behavior and specified there.)

The Object.assign compound-component pattern (e.g. `const Card = Object.assign(CardBase, { Header, Body })`) is not a distinct detection pattern in this spec: because the HOC-wrap check (AC-003) inspects only the call expression's first argument, `Object.assign(CardBase, { Header, Body })` is matched by the identical rule as any other single-first-argument call wrap. If `CardBase` is an already-collected component declared lexically earlier in the file, AC-003's outcome applies verbatim. If `CardBase` is not an already-collected component, AC-010's unmatched-binding outcome applies. No ComponentMapping entry is ever produced for the second argument's sub-properties (`Header`, `Body`) under any circumstance, and this specific omission is not tied to any diagnostic.
Cross-file type resolution — owned by resolver, out of scope for this module.
Output serialization formats — owned by types/output.rs and the serialization layer.

Default-value extraction (param_defaults / defaultProps merging) is out of scope for this spec: no criterion here specifies which shapes populate a ComponentMapping's param_defaults or how a `Component.defaultProps = {...}` static assignment merges into it. This is a real, exercised extractor behavior, just not one this spec's acceptance criteria cover — an implementer must not infer its rules from anything stated here.

Enum and const-array extraction (SourceData.enums and SourceData.const_arrays) — including TypeScript `enum` declarations, `as const` object/array literals, and variant-group helpers such as `cva`/`tv` calls, none of which are gated by the file being `.tsx` — is out of scope for this spec. No criterion here specifies their recognized shapes, keys, or values.
Import and export tracking (SourceData.imports and SourceData.exports) is out of scope for this spec: no criterion here specifies which import/export forms are recorded or in what shape.

Generic type-parameter tracking (SourceData.type_alias_params and SourceData.interface_type_params) is out of scope for this spec: no criterion here specifies how a generic interface's or type alias's own type parameters are recorded.

AC-023's nesting-counter guard: the exact starting offset and increment rule per distinct recursion entry path (e.g. whether a property's own top-level type, a generic type argument, or another entry point trips the guard at a slightly different chain depth near the ~200 threshold) is an internal implementation detail this spec does not assert a precise value for — only the externally observable outcome (one diagnostic per over-deep chain, truncation to source text, threshold near 200) is specified.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a .tsx file containing EITHER (a) a function component declared via a function DECLARATION (not a function expression assigned to a variable) — `function Card(props: CardProps) { ... }` — whose first parameter is a direct named-type reference, evaluated identically whether the declaration appears at the top level of the file or nested inside another function body (there is no top-level-only restriction on this pattern), OR (b) a PascalCase variable declarator whose own type annotation is one of the six recognized FC-family annotations — `FC`, `FunctionComponent`, `ComponentType`, `VFC`, `VoidFunctionComponent`, or `ForwardRefComponent` — each matched with or without a leading `React.` prefix (e.g. `React.FC<CardProps>`, `VFC<CardProps>`, `ComponentType<CardProps>`), whose first type argument is a direct named-type reference: SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for the declaration's name whose props type name is that referenced type's name — absent a qualifying `displayName` reassignment (position in the file relative to this declaration does not matter, per AC-027) targeting this same declaration's name, per AC-027, which supersedes the entry's key. For case (b), the match is driven entirely by the declarator's own type annotation; the initializer does not participate in the match and may be an arrow function, a function expression, any other expression, or absent entirely (see AC-025 for the no-initializer case). The referenced type name is recorded as-is and never resolved against a same-file declaration — it may be locally declared in this file or imported from elsewhere. A function EXPRESSION assigned to a PascalCase variable with no FC-family annotation (e.g. `const Card = function (props: CardProps) { return null; };`) does NOT match case (a) or (b) — see AC-010's example, which shows this shape's actual outcome.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding that does NOT carry one of AC-001's six FC-family type annotations, whose initializer is (after `as`-cast peeling, see AC-003's cast-peeling note) a call expression to `forwardRef` or `React.forwardRef` supplying two or more explicit type arguments, SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for that binding whose props type name is the call's second type argument — regardless of what the call's own argument is: an inline arrow function (`const Input = React.forwardRef<HTMLInputElement, InputProps>((props, ref) => ...)`), an inline function expression, or a bare identifier reference to an already-collected component declared earlier in the file (e.g. `function Render(props: RenderProps) { return null; } const Card = forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, CardProps>(Render);` yields `Card=>CardProps`, and `Render`'s own entry is NOT removed — this pattern never removes an entry, unlike AC-003/AC-005). If the call's second type argument is not a named-type reference but is instead an inline union, intersection, or object-literal type (e.g. `React.forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, { title: string }>(...)`), this criterion instead follows AC-024's anonymous-alias outcome — see AC-024. EXCLUSION: this criterion does NOT apply when the declarator also carries one of AC-001's six recognized FC-family type annotations — that annotation always takes precedence and supplies the props type name instead (e.g. `const X: React.FC<QProps> = React.forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, PProps>((p, r) => null);` yields `X=>QProps`, not `PProps`). This criterion takes precedence over AC-003 whenever the initializer is a forwardRef/React.forwardRef call with 2+ type arguments — see AC-003's exclusion clause. A `forwardRef`/`React.forwardRef` call with FEWER than two explicit type arguments does not match this criterion and is instead evaluated as an ordinary call expression under AC-003/AC-006/AC-007/AC-010.

CAST-PEELING NOTE (applies to this criterion and to AC-002, AC-005, AC-006, AC-007): before any initializer-shape test below is applied, any chain of `as` type-assertion expressions wrapping the initializer is peeled off, and the shape tests are applied to the innermost expression — `const A = memo(Base) as any as Foo;` is treated identically to `const A = memo(Base);`. (AC-001's FC-annotation path is unaffected: it reads the declarator's own type annotation, not the initializer, so no cast-peeling applies there.) EXCLUSION: this criterion (AC-003) does NOT apply when the call's callee is `forwardRef` or `React.forwardRef` and it supplies two or more explicit type arguments — that shape is AC-002's, which takes precedence and does not remove any entry. Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding whose (cast-peeled) initializer is a call expression, not matching AC-002's exclusion, whose FIRST argument is an identifier reference to any component that already has an entry in SourceData.component_mappings at the point this declarator is visited — regardless of which acceptance criterion produced that entry, including an entry produced by AC-003 or AC-005 itself (permitting alias chains, e.g. `function Base(props: BaseProps){} const A = memo(Base); const B = memo(A);` yields a final entry for `B` with props type `BaseProps`) — declared lexically earlier in the same file. Additional arguments beyond the first are ignored and do not prevent the match (e.g. `const Wrapped = withStyles(Card, options, more)` still matches). In the SourceData ultimately returned by parse_file(), SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for the wrapping binding whose props type name is the literal props type name carried by the referenced entry at visit time, and the referenced entry's own name is absent from that final SourceData — the underlying component's own entry is removed from the output — absent a qualifying `displayName` reassignment (position in the file relative to this declaration does not matter, per AC-027) targeting the wrapping binding's name, per AC-027, which supersedes the entry's key. (See AC-021 for the case where more than one binding aliases the same base component.)

Given a file containing a variable declared with no initializer whose type annotation is `React.ForwardRefExoticComponent<PropsType>` (or `ForwardRefExoticComponent<PropsType>`) — e.g. `declare const Icon: React.ForwardRefExoticComponent<IconProps>;` — where `IconProps` is a named type reference, recorded by name only and never resolved against a same-file declaration (it may be locally declared or imported), SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for `Icon` whose props type name is `IconProps`. Unlike AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, and AC-007, this pattern is NOT gated by file extension — it applies identically in a `.tsx`, `.ts`, or `.d.ts` file (see AC-008).

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding whose initializer is a bare identifier reference — no surrounding call expression — to any component that already has an entry in SourceData.component_mappings at the point this declarator is visited — regardless of which acceptance criterion produced that entry, including an entry produced by AC-003 or AC-005 itself (permitting alias chains) — declared lexically earlier in the same file, e.g. `const Button = InternalButton;`. In the SourceData ultimately returned by parse_file(), SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for `Button` whose props type name is the literal props type name that `InternalButton`'s entry carried at visit time (e.g. `InternalButtonProps`), and `InternalButton`'s own entry is absent from that final SourceData — absent a qualifying `displayName` reassignment (position in the file relative to this declaration does not matter, per AC-027) targeting `Button`, per AC-027, which supersedes the entry's key. This pattern is categorically distinct from AC-003 (HOC-wrap) by the absence of a call expression around the identifier. (See AC-021 for the case where more than one binding aliases the same base component.)

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding whose (cast-peeled, per AC-003's cast-peeling note) initializer is a call expression whose FIRST argument is an arrow function expression, an anonymous function expression, or a NAMED function expression whose own function name is PascalCase — in each case with a first parameter that is a direct named-type reference (recorded by name only, never resolved against a same-file declaration; it may be locally declared or imported) — SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for the wrapping binding whose props type name is that named type. Examples that match: `const Wrapped = withStyles(function Card(props: CardProps) { return null; })` (named, PascalCase), `const Wrapped = withStyles(function (props: CardProps) { return null; })` (anonymous), `const Wrapped = withStyles((props: CardProps) => null)` (arrow). A NAMED function expression whose own name is NOT PascalCase does NOT match this criterion — e.g. `const Wrapped = withStyles(function card(props: CardProps) { return null; });` produces no ComponentMapping for `Wrapped` and instead falls through to AC-010's unmatched-binding SkippedCandidate outcome, even though `card`'s own lowercase name is irrelevant to AC-015 (AC-015 governs top-level lowercase bindings, not inner function-expression names). Additional arguments to the outer call beyond the first are ignored and do not prevent the match.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding whose initializer is a call expression whose FIRST argument is itself a call expression to `forwardRef` or `React.forwardRef` supplying two or more explicit type arguments (e.g. `const Wrapped = memo(forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, XProps>((props, ref) => null))`), SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for `Wrapped` whose props type name is the nested forwardRef call's second type argument (e.g. `XProps`). Additional arguments to the outer call beyond the first are ignored and do not prevent the match.

Component detection via AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, and AC-007 is gated on the file's source type being JSX (a `.tsx` file) or a TypeScript declaration file (a `.d.ts` file); none of those six patterns produce a ComponentMapping entry in a plain `.ts` file (neither `.tsx` nor `.d.ts`) regardless of how many matching declarations it contains. AC-004 (the no-initializer `ForwardRefExoticComponent` shape) is the sole exception: it is NOT gated by file extension and produces a ComponentMapping in a plain `.ts` file exactly as it does in a `.tsx` or `.d.ts` file.

Given a .tsx file containing a type alias built from one of exactly five supported built-in generics — `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required`, or `Readonly` — where the generic's type arguments are malformed per the following rules: for `Omit` or `Pick`, fewer than two type arguments are supplied, or the first (base) type argument is not a resolvable type reference; for `Partial`, `Required`, or `Readonly`, fewer than one type argument is supplied, or the sole type argument is not a resolvable type reference — SourceData.diagnostics contains a diagnostic with code SkippedCandidate and Info severity identifying that alias's name; the alias is absent from SourceData.type_aliases and no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that name.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase-named variable binding whose declarator has an initializer that, after cast-peeling (per AC-003's cast-peeling note), matches none of AC-002 (forwardRef/React.forwardRef with 2+ type arguments), AC-001 (function declarations only, not expressions), AC-003 (identifier-first-argument call wrap), AC-005 (bare-identifier alias), AC-006 (inline function/arrow-first-argument call wrap with a PascalCase-or-anonymous function), or AC-007 (nested-forwardRef-first-argument call wrap) — for example `const Card = function (props: CardProps) { return null; };` (a function EXPRESSION, excluded by AC-001's declaration-only restriction), `const Widget = { render() {} };` (an object literal), or `const Wrapped = withStyles(function card(props: CardProps) { return null; });` (a named function-expression argument whose own name is lowercase, excluded by AC-006's PascalCase-or-anonymous restriction) — SourceData.diagnostics contains a diagnostic with code SkippedCandidate and Info severity identifying that binding's name; no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that name. (The no-initializer case is documented silent omission instead — see AC-016 — and is mutually exclusive with this criterion: AC-016 applies specifically to PascalCase bindings with no initializer at all, which never reach this SkippedCandidate wiring.)

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase-named function declaration with one or more parameters whose first parameter is EITHER untyped (no type annotation at all, e.g. `function Card(props) {...}`) OR typed with a primitive keyword type or any other shape that is not a type reference, a union, an intersection, or an inline object-literal type (e.g. `function Card(props: string) {...}`), SourceData.diagnostics contains a diagnostic with code SkippedCandidate and Info severity identifying that function's name; no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that name. A first parameter typed as a union, intersection, or inline object literal does NOT match this criterion — see AC-024 for that shape's actual outcome. (The zero-parameter case is treated as documented silent omission instead — see AC-017 — and is mutually exclusive with this criterion: AC-017 applies specifically to zero-param PascalCase function declarations, which never reach this SkippedCandidate wiring.)

Before AST parsing, the extractor scans the raw source bytes maintaining a single combined counter: any of the characters `{`, `(`, `[` increments it by one, and any of the characters `}`, `)`, `]` decrements it by one, with no pairing/matching check between a given opener and closer — the counter simply tracks aggregate open-vs-close character counts, saturating at zero so that surplus closing characters can never drive it negative. Characters inside comments (`//...` and `/*...*/`) and inside string or template literal contents are excluded from the scan entirely. If the maximum value this counter reaches during the scan is strictly greater than 2000 (2001 or more triggers; exactly 2000 does not), the extractor does not attempt AST parsing or component detection for that file. Instead, SourceData.diagnostics contains exactly one diagnostic with code ExcessiveNesting and Error severity, identifying the file path, and SourceData.component_mappings is empty for that file — no further per-declaration SkippedCandidate diagnostics are produced for that file, since the whole-file ExcessiveNesting diagnostic supersedes them.

Given a block comment whose end byte offset is within 120 bytes of the start byte offset of an immediately following component or props-type declaration (a raw byte-distance measurement over the entire gap — the gap's contents, whitespace or otherwise, are not filtered before measuring) and which has not already been attached to an earlier declaration, the comment is attached to that declaration's SourceData entry as follows: if and only if the comment's opening delimiter is the exact three-character sequence `/**` (a JSDoc-style comment), that `/**` opener and the trailing `*/` closer are stripped, and a single leading `*` (and one following space, if present) is stripped from each interior line; the resulting text up to (but not including) the first line beginning with `@` is stored in that declaration's `description` field, and each subsequent `@tag` line is parsed as `@tagName rest-of-line` and stored in that declaration's `tags` map (a `@param name description text` line is stored under the key `param:name`). If the comment's opener is a bare `/*` (not followed by a second `*`, i.e. an ordinary non-JSDoc block comment), the `/*` is NOT stripped and remains as the literal first two characters of the stored `description`; the `*/` closer is still stripped and the same `@`-tag truncation and stripping rules still apply to the remaining text. For example, `/**
 * Renders a button.
 * @param label the button label
 */` immediately preceding `function Button(props: ButtonProps) {` yields `description: "Renders a button."` and `tags: {"param:label": "the button label"}`, while `/* Renders a button. */` immediately preceding the same declaration yields `description: "/* Renders a button."` with the `/*` retained. EXCEPTION: for the AC-004 no-initializer `ForwardRefExoticComponent` shape, only `description` is ever populated from the associated comment; `tags` is always an empty map for that shape's entry even when the comment contains `@tag` lines — those lines are parsed and cause the comment to be marked consumed (making it unavailable to any later declaration) but their content is discarded rather than stored. A comment already attached to an earlier declaration is never attached to a second, later declaration (no double-consumption); the sole exception is a comment that yields both an empty `description` and an empty `tags` map, which is not marked as consumed and remains eligible to attach to a later declaration. There is no rule that an intervening declaration between the comment and the candidate blocks attachment — only the byte-distance threshold and the consumption rule govern eligibility.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase binding whose initializer is either a call expression with a first-argument identifier reference (AC-003's shape) or a bare identifier reference (AC-005's shape), where the referenced identifier names a PascalCase declaration that appears lexically LATER in the same file rather than earlier (a forward reference), no ComponentMapping entry is produced for the wrapping/aliasing binding, and SourceData.diagnostics contains a diagnostic with code SkippedCandidate and Info severity identifying that binding's name — the same outcome as AC-010, because the forward-referenced target is not yet an already-collected component at the point the wrapping/aliasing binding is visited.

Given a .tsx file containing a top-level `const` or `let` binding whose name starts with a lowercase letter and whose initializer would otherwise match the shape of a recognized component pattern (AC-001 through AC-007), no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that binding and SourceData.diagnostics contains no SkippedCandidate diagnostic referencing it — this silent omission is intended/documented behavior, not a defect.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase variable declared with no initializer and a type annotation that is neither `ForwardRefExoticComponent<...>` (see AC-004) nor any of AC-001's six FC-family annotation names (see AC-025) — e.g. `declare const Widget: SomeOtherType;` — no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that binding and SourceData.diagnostics contains no SkippedCandidate diagnostic referencing it — this silent omission is intended/documented behavior, not a defect.

Given a .tsx file containing a PascalCase-named function declaration with zero parameters (e.g. `function Placeholder() { return null; }`), no ComponentMapping entry is produced for that function and SourceData.diagnostics contains no SkippedCandidate diagnostic referencing it — this silent omission is intended/documented behavior, not a defect.

Given a props interface or type alias containing a computed key or a symbol-typed key (e.g. `interface Props { [key: string]: unknown; [Symbol.iterator]?: () => void; }`), those specific keys are omitted from the extracted prop list for that type — no diagnostic is emitted for the omission, and any other statically-named keys on the same interface/type are still extracted normally. A numeric-literal key (e.g. `0: string;`) is NOT omitted: it is extracted normally, with its decimal string form used as the prop name (the key `0` is extracted as prop name `"0"`).

Given a .tsx (or .ts) file with zero bytes of content, the extractor completes without error, producing a SourceData whose component_mappings, interfaces, type_aliases, enums, imports, exports, and diagnostics collections are all empty — an empty file is a valid input, not an error condition, and no diagnostic of any kind is emitted for it. As with AC-026, this criterion's emptiness assertion covers exactly those seven named fields; SourceData's remaining fields (type_alias_params, interface_type_params, const_arrays, and any param_defaults) are likewise empty for an empty file but are not independently asserted by any criterion in this spec.

For any input file processed by parse_file(), no reference borrowed from the OXC allocator/AST arena used during that call is retained in, or reachable from, the returned SourceData or any Diagnostic/ComponentMapping it contains — every string, name, and type reference in the returned SourceData is independently owned (e.g. String/CompactString) rather than a borrow tied to the arena's lifetime, so the arena can be dropped immediately after parse_file() returns without invalidating anything the caller holds.

Given a .tsx file containing N (N >= 2) distinct PascalCase bindings that each independently alias (per AC-003 or AC-005) the same already-collected base component declared lexically earlier in the file — e.g. `function Base(props: BaseProps) {} const A = Base; const Bcopy = Base;` — the SourceData ultimately returned by parse_file() contains a separate ComponentMapping entry for each of the N aliasing bindings, each carrying the base component's props type name (e.g. both `A` and `Bcopy` map to `BaseProps`), and the base component's own entry (`Base`) is absent from that SourceData — absent a qualifying `displayName` reassignment (position in the file relative to this declaration does not matter, per AC-027) targeting one of the N aliasing bindings, per AC-027, which supersedes that entry's key. No diagnostic is emitted for this case.

Given a source file with a RECOVERABLE parse error — one or more syntax errors that the parser reports without setting its panicked/fatal state, e.g. `type Bad = Partial<>; function Ok(props: OkProps) { return null; }` — SourceData.diagnostics contains one diagnostic with code ParseError and Error severity per parser error encountered, each identifying the file path, AND every other declaration in the file that parsed cleanly is extracted exactly as it would be in an error-free file (e.g. `Ok`'s ComponentMapping entry, `Ok=>OkProps`, is still present).

During the extractor's own recursive type-collection pass over a single top-level type annotation (independent of AC-012's pre-parse bracket-nesting guard, which operates on raw source bytes before parsing, has its own threshold, and produces a different diagnostic code and severity), a per-annotation nesting counter tracks descent depth and resets at the start of each new top-level type annotation (not cumulative across the file); once that counter exceeds a fixed threshold of 200 (MAX_TYPE_COLLECT_DEPTH) for a given node, the extractor stops descending into that node's subtree entirely and represents the subtree using its verbatim source text rather than a structured type breakdown, and a Warning-severity diagnostic with code MaxDepthExceeded (identifying the file path) is emitted for that node. For a SINGLE-CHILD nesting chain (each level has exactly one nested TSType descendant — e.g. `A<A<A<...>>>` via TSTypeReference's one type argument, `{ a: { a: { a: ... } } }` via nested TSTypeLiteral/property types, or TSArrayType/TSParenthesizedType chains), exactly ONE diagnostic is emitted for the whole chain, since only the first node to cross the threshold is visited before descent stops — a chain of 250 and a chain of 400 single-child-nested nodes both produce exactly one MaxDepthExceeded diagnostic apiece. This single-diagnostic guarantee does NOT extend to MULTI-CHILD TSType forms: a TSConditionalType node (`T extends U ? X : Y`) descends into up to four children (check_type, extends_type, true_type, false_type) simultaneously at the same depth, so a chained-conditional-type nesting form that crosses the threshold at its boundary level emits one diagnostic per child branch that individually crosses the threshold there — up to 4 for a single boundary-level TSConditionalType node, not 1. The rest of the type annotation outside any truncated subtree, and extraction of the rest of the enclosing file, both continue normally in every case — this guard does not abandon the file the way AC-012's guard does. The counter's exact starting offset and increment rule per distinct entry path (a property's own top-level type vs. a type argument inside a generic reference vs. other recursion entry points) is an internal implementation detail not asserted by this criterion — different entry paths may trip the guard at slightly different chain depths near the 200 threshold; see non_goals.

Given any of the following shapes where a props-type position that this spec otherwise requires to be a named-type reference is instead a union type, an intersection type, or an inline object-literal type — (a) a PascalCase-named function declaration's first parameter (AC-001's function-declaration path, e.g. `function Card(props: { title: string }) { return null; }` or `function Card(props: A | B) { return null; }`); (b) AC-001's own FC-family-annotation first type argument (AC-001's case (b) path, e.g. `const Card: React.FC<{ title: string }> = (props) => null;`) and AC-025's no-initializer equivalent of the same annotation path (e.g. `declare const Widget: React.FC<{ title: string }>;`) — both routed through the same shared type-name-extraction function as (a); (c) an inline function/arrow first-argument's first parameter inside a call-expression wrap (AC-006's shape, e.g. `const Wrapped = withStyles((props: { title: string }) => null)`); (d) a nested-forwardRef call's second type argument inside a call-expression wrap (AC-007's shape); or (e) a `forwardRef`/`React.forwardRef` call's own second type argument (AC-002's shape, e.g. `React.forwardRef<HTMLDivElement, { title: string }>(...)`) — SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for that declaration whose props type name is a synthesized placeholder of the form `__anon_N` (N is a non-negative integer, unique within the file), AND SourceData.type_aliases contains an entry keyed by the file-scoped form `${file_path}:__anon_N` (matching the same `path:Name` scoping convention used for every other entry in SourceData.type_aliases) representing the union/intersection/object-literal structure. No diagnostic is emitted for this case. (AC-003 and AC-005's identifier-alias shapes have no parameter or type-argument position of their own to synthesize from — they inherit whatever props type name, anonymous or named, the referenced entry already carries — so this criterion does not apply to them directly.)

Given a `.tsx` or `.d.ts` file containing a PascalCase variable declared with no initializer whose type annotation is one of AC-001's six FC-family annotation names (`FC`, `FunctionComponent`, `ComponentType`, `VFC`, `VoidFunctionComponent`, `ForwardRefComponent`, each with or without a leading `React.` prefix) supplying a first type argument that is a direct named-type reference — e.g. `declare const Widget: React.FC<WidgetProps>;` — SourceData.component_mappings contains an entry for `Widget` whose props type name is `WidgetProps`. This pattern is gated by file extension identically to AC-001, AC-002, AC-003, AC-005, AC-006, and AC-007 (`.tsx` and `.d.ts` on, plain `.ts` off): the same annotation on the same no-initializer declaration in a plain `.ts` file produces NO ComponentMapping entry, because `try_fc_annotation` is only reachable when the file's source type is JSX or a TypeScript declaration file. AC-004 (the `ForwardRefExoticComponent` no-init shape) remains the sole pattern in this spec that is NOT gated by file extension — see AC-008.

Given a source file with a FATAL parse error — a syntax error severe enough that the parser sets its panicked/fatal state, e.g. `function Card(props: Props) { return ;;; ) }` — SourceData.diagnostics contains one diagnostic with code ParseError and Error severity per parser error encountered, each identifying the file path, AND the resulting SourceData's component_mappings, interfaces, type_aliases, enums, imports, and exports are all empty for that file, including for any declaration that appears lexically before the fatal error and would otherwise have parsed cleanly on its own. This criterion enumerates the SourceData collections it asserts are empty exhaustively for those seven named fields (component_mappings, interfaces, type_aliases, enums, imports, exports, plus diagnostics which is non-empty per above); SourceData's remaining fields (type_alias_params, interface_type_params, const_arrays, and per-mapping param_defaults) are likewise empty in this case but are not independently asserted by any criterion in this spec — see the new non_goals entry on those fields.

Given a .tsx file containing a component declaration recognized by any of AC-001 through AC-007, AC-024, or AC-025 under some name `X` (present in SourceData.component_mappings at the point the whole file has been walked), and a static-member assignment of the exact form `X.displayName = "NewName"` where the right-hand side is a SINGLE STRING LITERAL (single- or double-quoted; a template literal — e.g. `` X.displayName = `NewName`; `` — does NOT match, even one with no interpolated expressions, and the assignment is left with no effect on X's entry) appearing anywhere in the file — its lexical position relative to X's own declaration does not matter, since this rule is applied only after the whole file has been walked, not at the point either statement is visited — the SourceData ultimately returned by parse_file() contains no entry keyed by `X`; that entry is instead present keyed by `NewName`, carrying the same props type name `X`'s entry carried before the reassignment was applied. If two or more distinct `displayName` reassignments target the same original name `X` in the same file, only the FIRST (lexically earliest in file-scan order) reassignment's target name is present in the final SourceData — the first rename changes the mapping's key away from `X`, so a second, later reassignment's own lookup for `X` finds no matching entry and has no effect; this is a consequence of the rename being applied via a single first-match lookup per pending rename, in file-scan order, not a distinct rule requiring separate verification. A `displayName` assignment whose right-hand side is not a string literal (e.g. a variable reference or a template literal) produces no rename and no diagnostic. A `displayName` assignment whose left-hand object name does not match any name currently present in SourceData.component_mappings at rename time produces no rename, no diagnostic, and no error.

AC-023 (and a new non_goals entry) drops the specific 201-vs-202 counter-value claim entirely, since v7's own replacement values were themselves gate-falsified on both branches in round 6 — after three consecutive rounds of a new precise-but-wrong value replacing the last, this criterion is deliberately degraded to assert only the externally observable outcome (one diagnostic per over-deep chain, ~200 threshold, truncation-to-source-text) and explicitly disclaims asserting the exact per-entry-path starting offset as an internal implementation detail, mirroring how SPEC-PIPELINE-001's AC-001 was similarly degraded after its own repeated precision failures on ignore-crate internals.
